summary_paragraph: A man with end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis, type 2 diabetes, atrial fibrillation, and a history of steal syndrome was admitted from his extended care facility due to fatigue and malaise after missing a dialysis session. He presented with hyperkalemia and fluid overload, confirmed by elevated potassium and pulmonary edema on chest X-ray. He received timely hemodialysis, which improved his electrolytes and respiratory status. During the admission, he experienced narcotic-induced encephalopathy, which resolved after dose reduction. Pain management was optimized with palliative care input, transitioning to once-daily OxyContin and lower PRN oxycodone to balance analgesia and sedation. He briefly considered discontinuing dialysis but ultimately chose to continue. His atrial fibrillation was managed with increased diltiazem after an episode of rapid ventricular rate, and insulin was adjusted due to hypoglycemia from poor intake. He was discharged to extended care with stable vital signs, improved mental status, and clear instructions on weight monitoring and medication safety.
